Inter-college and interdisciplinary teams are allowed. Team composition cannot be changed after registration. Domains Mechavers: Robotics, Drones & Autonomous Systems Silicore: FPGA, VLSI & Reconfigurable Computing Wavenex: Wireless Communication, RF & Signal Processing Neuronix: Edge AI, Embedded Intelligence & Deep Tech Nexusgrid: Industrial Automation & Critical Infrastructure Circuitshield: Hardware Security & Cyber-Physical Defence A hardware prototype is mandatory in every domain. Round 2: 36-Hour Prototype Challenge Shortlisted teams build, test and demonstrate a functional hardware prototype on the DSU campus. Each team must work on one problem statement. Final submissions must include the prototype, circuit diagram, code repository link and a one-page report. The final demonstration consists of 5 minutes of presentation and 3 minutes of Q&A. Evaluation Criteria Innovation: originality and creativity of the idea Technical Feasibility: practical implementation and scalability Real-World Relevance and Presentation: alignment with the problem and clarity of communication Awards and Perks Winner Runner-up Second Runner-up Best Innovation Best Hardware Integration Most Cost-Effective Solution Participation certificates for all participants Goodies and an industry-expert meetup What We Provide Food and refreshments, internet and power supply at the venue, and transport for shortlisted teams between Silk Institute Metro Station and DSU Main Campus. At least one team member must be present at the venue at all times. All submissions must meet the prescribed deadlines. Participants must follow safety guidelines and organiser instructions. The decisions of the judges and organising committee are final. Join VIDYUTSPANDA’26 to innovate, collaborate, and turn ideas into working hardware solutions!

raw.details:
VIDYUTSPANDA’26 is a 36-hour hardware innovation challenge organised by the Department of Electronics & Communication Engineering, Dayananda Sagar University, Bengaluru, in association with Electroblitz Club and IEEE DSU Student Branch. Participants build working hardware prototypes that solve real-world problems, guided by industry mentors and academic experts.

  • Event dates: 19-20 November 2026
  • Venue: Dayananda Sagar University, Harohalli, Bengaluru
  • Team size: exactly 3 members
  • Registration fee: ₹300 per team
  • Registration deadline: 10 November 2026

Eligibility

  • Open to students from all colleges and disciplines.
  • Each team must have exactly 3 members.
  • Each team must include at least one B.Tech student. Teams made up entirely of M.Tech students are not permitted.
  • Inter-college and interdisciplinary teams are allowed.
  • Team composition cannot be changed after registration.

Domains

  • Mechavers: Robotics, Drones & Autonomous Systems
  • Silicore: FPGA, VLSI & Reconfigurable Computing
  • Wavenex: Wireless Communication, RF & Signal Processing
  • Neuronix: Edge AI, Embedded Intelligence & Deep Tech
  • Nexusgrid: Industrial Automation & Critical Infrastructure
  • Circuitshield: Hardware Security & Cyber-Physical Defence

A hardware prototype is mandatory in every domain.

Competition Format

Round 1: PPT Screening
Submit a PPT outlining your problem statement, proposed solution, innovation and technical feasibility on the official template.

Round 2: 36-Hour Prototype Challenge
Shortlisted teams build, test and demonstrate a functional hardware prototype on the DSU campus.

Each team must work on one problem statement. Final submissions must include the prototype, circuit diagram, code repository link and a one-page report. The final demonstration consists of 5 minutes of presentation and 3 minutes of Q&A.

Evaluation Criteria

  • Innovation: originality and creativity of the idea
  • Technical Feasibility: practical implementation and scalability
  • Real-World Relevance and Presentation: alignment with the problem and clarity of communication

Awards and Perks

  • Winner
  • Runner-up
  • Second Runner-up
  • Best Innovation
  • Best Hardware Integration
  • Most Cost-Effective Solution
  • Participation certificates for all participants
  • Goodies and an industry-expert meetup

What We Provide

Food and refreshments, internet and power supply at the venue, and transport for shortlisted teams between Silk Institute Metro Station and DSU Main Campus.

Rules

  • Teams must have exactly three members.
  • Original work is mandatory. Plagiarism and previously developed code are prohibited.
  • All project work must be done during the event, at the venue.
  • Participants must bring their own laptops, components and development kits.
  • Pre-built modules are prohibited, except standard sensors and microcontrollers.
  • At least one team member must be present at the venue at all times.
  • All submissions must meet the prescribed deadlines.
  • Participants must follow safety guidelines and organiser instructions.
  • The decisions of the judges and organising committee are final.

Join VIDYUTSPANDA’26 to innovate, collaborate, and turn ideas into working hardware solutions!
